questions.question: The transmission of genetic programs requires a copying step and which other step?
questions.explanation: The transmission of genetic programs requires a copying step and a distribution step.

questions.question: The sequence of events by which a cell duplicates its genome and eventually divides into two daughter cells is termed what?
questions.explanation: This sequence of events is termed the cell cycle.

questions.question: The cell cycle occurs between the completion of one mitotic division and the completion of what?
questions.explanation: It occurs between the completion of one mitotic division and the completion of the next division.

questions.question: Cellular checkpoints mechanisms are strictly put under control to avoid undue growth that may result in what?
questions.explanation: Undue growth and multiplications of cells may result in cancer.

questions.question: In the nucleus of a eukaryotic cell, the distribution process of parental genetic materials occurs in mitosis and which other process?
questions.explanation: The distribution process occurs in two ways: mitosis and meiosis.

questions.question: Cells divide for three major reasons critical to survival: growth, repair, and what else?
questions.explanation: Cells divide for growth, repair, and reproduction.

questions.question: The increase in the number of cells in an organism due to mitosis results in what?
questions.explanation: Growth is a result of mitosis.

questions.question: Humans start off as one single cell, and by the time they are adults, they have over how many trillion cells?
questions.explanation: Adults have over 10 trillion cells.

questions.question: If tissue is damaged, which process becomes extremely important for replacing old cells?
questions.explanation: Repair is extremely important if tissue is damaged.

questions.question: Asexual reproduction occurs when there is only one parent and results from which type of division?
questions.explanation: Asexual reproduction results from normal cell division, mitosis.

questions.question: Sexual reproduction requires offspring to have a combination of both parents' genetic material and occurs only by which process?
questions.explanation: Sexual reproduction can only occur by meiosis.

questions.question: Cells can divide mitotically to create more surface area for which function?
questions.explanation: Cells divide to create more surface area for waste disposal.

questions.question: Interphase constitutes the main phase of the cell cycle in which the cell spends the majority of its time and performs what percentage of its purposes?
questions.explanation: The interphase lasts more than 95% of the duration of the cell cycle.

questions.question: The G1 phase is the interval between mitosis and initiation of what process?
questions.explanation: G1 phase is the interval between mitosis and initiation of DNA replication.

questions.question: During the S phase, the amount of DNA per cell doubles from 2C to what?
questions.explanation: If the initial amount of DNA is denoted as 2C then it increases to 4C.

questions.question: The G2 phase is also called pre-mitotic or what other phase?
questions.explanation: G2 phase is also called pre-mitotic or post-synthetic phase.

questions.question: Cells that do not divide further exit G1 phase to enter an inactive stage called what?
questions.explanation: Cells that do not divide further exit G1 to enter the quiescent stage.

questions.question: Mitosis is an asexual form of cell division where a parent cell produces two daughter cells with the same what?
questions.explanation: Mitosis produces two daughter cells with the same genetic component.

questions.question: Mitosis is divided into four stages of nuclear division which include prophase, metaphase, anaphase, and what?
questions.explanation: The four stages are prophase, metaphase, anaphase, and telophase.

questions.question: The phrase "People Meet And Talk" is used to remember the sequence of which stages?
questions.explanation: The phrase helps remember the sequence of the mitotic stages.

questions.question: Which stage of mitosis begins with the appearance of chromatin fibers as long slender threads?
questions.explanation: Prophase begins with the appearance of chromatin fibers.

questions.question: In metaphase, the chromosomes migrate to which plane in the midline of the cell?
questions.explanation: Chromosomes migrate to the equatorial plane in the midline of the cell.

questions.question: The spindle fibers bind to a small disc-shaped structure at the surface of the centromeres called what?
questions.explanation: Spindle fibers bind to a small disc-shaped structure called kinetochore.

questions.question: Anaphase is described as which stage of mitosis?
questions.explanation: Anaphase is the shortest stage of mitosis.

questions.question: In telophase, the cytoplasm begins to constrict and the cell starts to pinch-in at the centre forming what structure in animal cells?
questions.explanation: The cell starts to pinch-in forming a furrow in animal cells.

questions.question: Cytokinesis is the division of a cell into daughter cells and follows which phase?
questions.explanation: Cytokinesis follows telophase.

questions.question: In plant cells, what structure forms from materials supplied by Golgi vesicles during cytokinesis?
questions.explanation: A cell plate forms from materials supplied by Golgi vesicles.

questions.question: Mitosis is responsible for replacement of dead or worn out cells and is the major component in asexual and what other type of reproduction?
questions.explanation: It is the major component in asexual and artificial reproduction.

questions.question: Examples of organisms that use mitosis for artificial reproduction include budding in yeast and what other process?
questions.explanation: Binary fission in bacteria is an example of mitosis in reproduction.

questions.question: Meiosis is a reduction division involving one diploid parent cell dividing to produce how many haploid daughter cells?
questions.explanation: Meiosis produces four haploid daughter cells.

questions.question: Meiosis consists of how many cell divisions?
questions.explanation: Meiosis consists of two cell divisions: meiosis I and meiosis II.

questions.question: As with mitosis, interphase occurs prior to meiosis and DNA replication occurs how many times?
questions.explanation: DNA replication occurs only once prior to the two divisions in meiosis.

questions.question: Meiosis I is referred to as the reduction division because the chromosome number is reduced from 46 to what in humans?
questions.explanation: The chromosome number is reduced from 46 to 23 in humans.

questions.question: The first meiotic division consists of four stages: prophase I, metaphase I, anaphase I, and what?
questions.explanation: Meiosis I consists of telophase I as its final stage.

questions.question: Prophase I has been further subdivided into five phases based on what?
questions.explanation: Prophase I is subdivided based on chromosomal behaviour.

questions.question: During which stage of prophase I do homologous chromosomes become closely associated to form pairs?
questions.explanation: Homologous chromosomes become closely associated during zygotene.

questions.question: The pairing of homologous chromosomes during zygotene is referred to as what?
questions.explanation: The pairing of homologous chromosomes is referred to as synapsis.

questions.question: During which stage of prophase I does crossing over between non-sister chromatids occur?
questions.explanation: Pachytene is characterized by crossing over between non-sister chromatids.

questions.question: The enzyme involved in the process of crossing over is called what?
questions.explanation: The enzyme involved in crossing over is called recombinase.

questions.question: The X-shaped structures formed during crossing over are called what?
questions.explanation: Crossing over forms X-shaped chiasmata.

questions.question: In metaphase I, the bivalent chromosomes align on which structure?
questions.explanation: Bivalent chromosomes align on the equatorial plate.

questions.question: The chiasmata hold which structures together during metaphase I?
questions.explanation: Chiasmata hold sister chromatids together during metaphase I.

questions.question: During anaphase I, the homologous chromosomes in each bivalent are separated and move to where?
questions.explanation: Homologous chromosomes move to opposite poles of the cell.

questions.question: In anaphase I, microtubules pull the homologous chromosomes apart, but which structures are held together?
questions.explanation: Sister chromatids are held together during anaphase I.

questions.question: During telophase I, the nuclear membrane and nucleolus reappear, and which process begins?
questions.explanation: Cytokinesis begins during telophase I.

questions.question: Meiosis II is initiated immediately after cytokinesis and is similar to which process?
questions.explanation: The process of meiosis II is the same as the process of mitosis.

questions.question: In which stage of meiosis II is there a splitting of centromere and separation of sister chromatids?
questions.explanation: It is in meiosis II that there is a splitting of centromere and separation of sister chromatids.

questions.question: During prophase II, chromosomes begin to condense, nuclear membrane dissolves, and what other structures are formed?
questions.explanation: Spindle fibers are formed during prophase II.

questions.question: In metaphase II, chromosomes line up in which part of the cell?
questions.explanation: Chromosomes line up in the center of the cell during metaphase II.

questions.question: Meiosis increases genetic variation in the population and makes which type of reproduction possible?
questions.explanation: Meiosis makes sexual reproduction possible.
